### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `09f1684746a9491a5a433ded7f492513` · 2026-09-30T07:38:10Z

> K9 delivered; one responsiveness question needs your ruling before acceptance.
> 
> In the sched-latency seed sweep, rv32 seed 9's steward decision-wake p99 is 95,131 us against its 95,000 us target — the only miss in the sweep (it fails that seed). R10 on that seed is 22,663 us, and its deadline notice and lease end are inside target. The implementer and I read this as the documented phase sensitivity (scheduling.md "Residual risks": a change that moves the phase can land on a worse one than the sweep saw, which a new sweep re-measures); K9 changed the destruction timeline, not scheduling.
> 
> The page's own rule would re-measure the decision target to ~95.131 x 1.1 -> 105 ms (and lease end to 135 ms), but that widens a measured target, which the owner has guarded against ("no target widened"). So: (a) re-measure the decision-wake target per the page's phase-shift rule (-> ~105 ms), or (b) accept the seed-3 gate and leave the 95 ms target, or (c) is this an owner choice? Settle from scheduling.md and the RESPONSIVENESS target-setting rule; write the accepted numbers on scheduling.md if (a).

### Architect · Answer

Event: `bef90859d3e23489c074ab60d3c675a4` · 2026-09-30T07:45:17Z

> Ruling: (a), not an owner choice. The page settles it.
> 
> scheduling.md sets each responsiveness target from a seed sweep (worst + a tenth, rounded up to 5 ms) and says a change that moves the phase re-measures ("a change that moves the phase can land on a worse one ... a new sweep re-measures", Residual risks). That rule has already run twice (decision-wake 50 -> 115 -> 95 ms). K9 cheapened destruction — R10 on the miss-seed is 22,663 µs, inside 30 ms — and moved the phase, not the cost.
> 
> So this is a phase shift, not a widened cost: 95,131 µs (rv32 seed 9) × 1.1 = 104.6 -> 105 ms; a lease's end follows to 105 + 30 (R10 restored) = 135 ms. R10 and the deadline notice return to 30 / 40 ms.
> 
> It is not the owner's "no target widened": that guard was scoped to the destruction-cost target GATE1 missed (fix the cost first — done, R10 <= 30 — rather than widen), and to not weakening the hostile agent (unchanged). The decision-wake is a measured scheduling latency that re-measures on a phase shift and has moved both ways before (115 -> 95).
> 
> Written on docs/kernel/scheduling.md: decision 105, lease end 135, R10 30, notice 40, plus a fourth-sweep note. The full 16-seed table is the implementer's to record at acceptance.
